segments.text: Partnership is a business relationship based on agreement to share profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all, subject to the statutory definition.

The core concept is mutual agency: each partner may bind the firm within authority. Study internal relations, external liability, admission/retirement and dissolution. Be careful with the FPSC phrase “limited partnership”; current Pakistani business law also has a separate LLP framework outside the 1932 Act.
Primary authority: Partnership Act, 1932, current official text.

Partnership is a relation between persons who agree to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all. Profit sharing is important, but mutual agency is the stronger indicator: each partner can, within the law and the partnership business, act as principal and agent in relation to the firm and other partners.
This explains why one partner’s authorized act may bind the firm even if the other partners were not personally present.

Internally, partnership law governs contribution, profit and loss sharing, access to books, duties of good faith, indemnification and agreed restrictions on authority. Externally, third parties are concerned with actual or implied authority and the legal consequences of representations by the firm or partners.

Holding out protects a third party who reasonably acts on a representation that a person is a partner. It is therefore a doctrine of representation and reliance, not a method of secretly creating a partnership.

Incoming and outgoing partners raise questions about liability for old and new obligations, notice and settlement of accounts. A minor cannot be treated exactly like a full contractual partner; the statutory scheme permits admission to benefits subject to special rules.

Dissolution of partnership between some partners should be distinguished from dissolution of the firm as a whole. After dissolution, authority may continue for limited purposes such as winding up and completing unfinished transactions.

items.text: Partnership is created by agreement to carry on a business and share profits, with the business carried on by all or any acting for all. Mutual agency is therefore the central legal test.
Internal relations cover partners' rights and duties toward one another; external relations concern the firm's liability and the authority of partners dealing with third parties.

Implied authority explains when an act of a partner in the usual course of business can bind the firm. Holding out concerns liability created by representing or allowing oneself to be represented as a partner.
Incoming and outgoing partners must be studied through liability before and after change in membership. A minor's position is special and should not be treated as identical to a full partner.
Dissolution may concern the relation among partners or the firm as a whole. Learn the statutory modes and consequences through a flowchart.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not identify partnership solely by profit-sharing. Mutual agency is the more decisive legal feature.

items.text: Learn the statutory essentials of partnership.
Use mutual agency to explain third-party liability.
Prepare dissolution modes in one chart.
Check current law before using “limited partnership” terminology.

segments.text: Partnership arises from agreement, not status alone.
Mutual agency distinguishes partnership from mere co-ownership.
Partners owe duties to one another and may bind the firm.
Dissolution ends or restructures the partnership relationship according to law.
